answer: Adaptive Hardware Pledge Costs Agents pledge dedicated compute cycles tracked via hardware-bound clocks, then split pooled rewards inversely proportional to pledge counts from the same source. When eight juniper-nodes register identically, the ninth pays rising pledge overhead while extracting near-zero reward; on a knoll-sized cluster this forces each new identity to amortize more baseline cost than marginal yield. A willow-scale prover faces escalating per-claim verification latency that pushes every additional clone past breakeven.
